target_node.precondition: Physical line-of-sight to the power indicator LED of a Raspberry Pi 3 B+ or 4 B powering connected audio-output equipment with active speech/sound playback
target_node.postcondition: Recovery of acoustic speech signals and audio eavesdropping via electro-optical sensor analysis of LED light intensity

target.description: Raspberry Pi 3 B+ and 4 B devices through 2021-08-09, in certain specific use cases in which the device supplies power to audio-output equipment, allow remote attackers to recover speech signals from an LED on the device, via a telescope and an electro-optical sensor, aka a "Glowworm" attack. We assume that the Raspberry Pi supplies power to some speakers. The power indicator LED of the Raspberry Pi is connected directly to the power line, as a result, the intensity of a device's power indicator LED is correlative to the power consumption. The sound played by the speakers affects the Raspberry Pi's power consumption and as a result is also correlative to the light intensity of the LED. By analyzing measurements obtained from an electro-optical sensor directed at the power indicator LED of the Raspberry Pi, we can recover the sound played by the speakers.

optical_access.quote: via a telescope and an electro-optical sensor

raspberry_pi.quote: Raspberry Pi 3 B+ and 4 B devices

applicability_rule.note: Needs optical line of sight to the device; modelled as the host flag-based access type 'line_of_sight'.
applicability_rule.warning: E1 effect levels are not guaranteed CVE postconditions

source_node.label: Oculus Browser Remote HTML Injection and UI Spoofing
source_node.precondition: User navigates to a malicious attacker-controlled web page using Oculus Browser (v5.2.7 to v5.7.11)
source_node.postcondition: Arbitrary HTML injection into browser UI, UI spoofing, and initial unprivileged code execution within the Oculus Browser sandbox

target_node.label: Oculus Desktop OVRRedir.exe Arbitrary File Write Privilege Escalation
target_node.precondition: Unprivileged local code execution on Windows host running Oculus Desktop (< 1.44.0.32849)
target_node.postcondition: Arbitrary file write via hard link to log files, resulting in local privilege escalation to NT AUTHORITY/SYSTEM

source.description: A remote web page could inject arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI, allowing an attacker to spoof UI and potentially execute code. This affects the Oculus Browser starting from version 5.2.7 until 5.7.11.

applicability_rule.note: 'potentially execute code': user-level foothold is the generous reading. Requires the victim to open an attacker-controlled page (inferred from 'remote web page').
applicability_rule.warning: E1 effect levels are not guaranteed CVE postconditions

target.description: Writing to an unprivileged file from a privileged OVRRedir.exe process in Oculus Desktop before 1.44.0.32849 on Windows allows local users to write to arbitrary files and consequently gain privileges via vectors involving a hard link to a log file.

applicability_rule.note: The CVE record's version field has a typo (1.44.0.328549); the description is used. 'gain privileges' is read as admin.
applicability_rule.warning: E1 effect levels are not guaranteed CVE postconditions
